Analysis by Richard Cowan 

Regarding fascism,see 

George Will Quotes The Czar Quoting Lincoln and Quotes The Czar Lying, So I Will Quote George Will. And A Few Others. 

Although Europe is generally moving away from cannabis prohibition, that is not true everywhere. 

Last week, the Italian equivalent of the Supreme Court, their Corte di Cassazione, ruled that growing just one cannabis plant, even for personal use, was a serious crime and could result in a sentence ranging from six to twenty years in prison! 

Unfortunately, this ruling came just after the election of a far right government, returning Silvio Berlusconi to power and virtually wiping out the Italian Left. 

Yesterday, Gianni Alemanno, a Berlusconi ally and “former” neo-fascist was elected mayor of Rome. (Alemanno left the neo-fascist “Italian Socialist Movement” to join Berlusconi's “People of Freedom” party. Ironic names?) Consequently, there is no prospect of any legislative or administrative restraint, and it is likely that the situation will only get worse. From 2006, see 

Kubby Update; Overgrow.com Overthrown; Italian Fascists Renew War on Cannabis; New Canadian Justice Minister Is Ashcroft-lite; NORML Report on Reefer Madness. 

Italy is a political and economic basket case, so their cannabis policies are not likely to be noticed elsewhere, but it is going to be a difficult few years for our friends there. Roman Reefer Madness The Vatican Commits a Mortal Sin, But Spain Just Says, “No!” Forgive Them Father, For They Know Not What They Do. (But They Should!)

Speaking of economic and political basket cases and (leftwing) fascism, the UK Labour government, which has never seen a civil liberty that it likes, is set to reclassify cannabis – again – back to Class B with meth and barbiturates – from Class C with valium and most benzodiazepine tranquilizers and steroids. In other words, from dumb to dumber.

See 

Beyond Bonkers: UK "Reclassification" Of Cannabis Caps Weeks of Absurdity. Prime Minister Has A Drug Problem? 

It has long been clear that Prime Minister Gordon Brown was going to ignore the final report from the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs (ACMD) which was delivered to the Home Office today. The ACMD which includes doctors, police, judges and drug counselors has been reported to oppose reclassification, so when the government thumbs its nose at these experts, they may resign in protest. 

One of the most outspoken opponents of cannabis prohibition on the ACMD, Professor Leslie Iversen, an Oxford University pharmacologist, has warned that if the ACMD’s advice is ignored "it would call into question the whole function and future of this group."

See 

Oxford Pharmacologist, Fellow of the Prestigious Royal Society, Says Marijuana Safer Than Aspirin. 

Of course, there is a long tradition of ignoring reports on cannabis that don’t support the prohibitionist party line. 

See 

Bush’s New Freedom Initiative: “Treatment” For Using Cannabis, From The Wonderful Folks Who Brought Us Vioxx, Baycol, Etc. Author of IOM Report Says, "I can't understand why it isn't rescheduled." 

Nixon ignored the Schafer report in 1972, just as Roosevelt ignored the LaGuardia report in 1944, etc. 

See 

NORML Compares WHO Suppression of Cannabis Study to the Suppression of Previous Favorable Studies 

Meanwhile, even in The Netherlands prohibitionist stupidity is taking its toll. Despite opposition from Amsterdam, the Parliament seems set to ban the sale of fresh “magic” mushrooms. The sale of dried mushrooms is already illegal in the estimated 350 “Smart Shops.” I very much regret this decision, but it is likely to cause a lot of protests that will strengthen the Dutch anti-prohibitionists. 

See 

NORML Sensible Amsterdam Tour A Success. So Is The Coffee Shop System. Seeing Freedom Work.
